concerns.asked: Explain in the main text how the critical currents are extracted, and show that out-of-plane field, misalignment and self-field effects do not produce the in-plane diode signal.
concerns.response: A new main-text subsection defines I_c± as extrema over narrow B_perp sweeps (Eqs. 1a-b) and explains why this removes flux modulation. It notes that B_perp+ and B_perp- differ because of asymmetric J_c(x), and keeps B_perp within the central lobe to avoid trapping vortices (p2). New Fig. 1c-g shows the Fraunhofer and gate maps and zooms at B_par = -125, 0 and +125 mT (p3).
concerns.judgment: The likely request was met: the procedure is now explicit, justified and illustrated with raw data.
concerns.still_open: Maps are shown for one representative device only, with no test that eta or B_eta survive a change of B_perp window. The W_sc -> infinity device uses a different smoothing procedure.

changes.summary: New subsection and Eqs. 1a-b on out-of-plane field

concerns.asked: Measure the diode efficiency with the in-plane field parallel to the current, where the intended mechanisms predict little effect.
concerns.response: Fig. 1h compares eta(B_par) at theta = 0 and theta = pi/2, with one-standard-deviation bands. The theta = 0 band includes a possible 2 degree misalignment, and a new supplementary section covers the longitudinal diode effect (p3, p6).
concerns.judgment: The control was added. From the caption, it is the null comparison a referee would ask for.
concerns.still_open: It is shown for one representative device, not for the narrowest and widest contacts, so it does not test whether the W_sc trends themselves come from the intended mechanisms.

concerns.asked: Give the measurement conditions and the definition of I_c, and add uncertainties to the extracted quantities.
concerns.response: Methods now gives a 30 mK base temperature, the bias and readout chain, switching-current sweeps, and an uncertainty from the rms deviation of the local fit, propagated into eta (p2, p6). B* has fit standard errors in Figs. 3c and 4, and eta has shaded bands in Fig. 5a (p4-5).
concerns.judgment: The protocol and a basic uncertainty estimate are now there. Error bars are still missing on the quantities behind the main claims: I_c(W_sc) in Fig. 3b, max eta in Fig. 5b and B_eta in Fig. 5c.
concerns.still_open: Switching-distribution widths, sweep-direction checks and uncertainties on xi and the Fig. 5c fit are still not given.

changes.summary: Error bars on B*, bands on eta

concerns.asked: Say what the W_sc -> infinity device is and why it represents the infinite-width limit.
concerns.response: The leads of this device are not etched, and the nearest superconductor-insulator edge is tens of microns away, far beyond the coherence length (p2). Its data come from a separate smoothing procedure described in the SI (p2).
concerns.judgment: The definition the request asked for is given and is reasonable.
concerns.still_open: Why this device departs from the linear B_eta trend still rests on an unsupported Josephson-vortex remark.

changes.summary: Definition of the W_sc -> infinity device

concerns.asked: Justify physically why finite contact width suppresses I_c as in Eq. 1, including what happens at the rear edge of the contact, and consider other finite-size effects.
concerns.response: The rear edge is now an S/N interface where Cooper pairs are Andreev-reflected into normal current, and the Al etch is said to stop at the semiconductor (p2). The text adds that the dirty-limit agreement means correlations propagate diffusively, and a caveat on confinement effects as W_sc -> 0 (p2-3).
concerns.judgment: The physical picture is clearer and the boundary is now stated. The model is still heuristic, and xi still has no uncertainty.
concerns.still_open: The amplitude-versus-probability argument, the tau = 1 and phase = pi assumption and the uncertainty on xi are unchanged.

changes.summary: Andreev reflection at a distal S/N interface

concerns.asked: Report whether there is nonreciprocity at zero field, which would point to a field offset or another source of symmetry breaking.
concerns.response: The text now states that eta(0) is zero within experimental uncertainty, so the applied field is the only source of time-reversal breaking (p4).
concerns.still_open: How the zero of B_par was calibrated is still not described.

concerns.asked: Give the growth, transport characterization and fabrication details, including the etch geometry.
concerns.response: New Methods sections describe the heterostructure growth, with layers bottom to top and van der Pauw mobility, density and mean free path, and the fabrication steps with etchants and depths (p6). The main text adds the etch end points (p2).
concerns.judgment: The details are now there, but they introduce an inconsistency to fix.
concerns.still_open: Methods gives n = 8.14e11 cm^-2 and l = 147 nm, while the coherence-length estimate uses n = 6e12 cm^-2 and l = 130 nm (p2-3, p6).

concerns.asked: Place the study against earlier work that varied junction geometry.
concerns.response: The introduction adds that few experiments have systematically varied contact width, citing Haxell et al. (p1).
concerns.judgment: This is a small framing addition that fits a novelty or context request.

concerns.asked: Clarify how orbital and spin-orbit mechanisms are distinguished, and how the estimated fields relate to the measured B_eta.
concerns.response: The estimated extremal fields are renamed B_eta, a note on the neglected second Fermi surface is added (p5), and the Conclusion says the relative contributions vary with gate, field and W_sc (p6).
concerns.judgment: The changes go the asked way but are small. The orbital attribution, the Fig. 5c fit and the saturation claim are unchanged, so any pushback was likely answered in the response letter.
concerns.still_open: The fit fixes only the product Phi*d, and the estimated fields miss the data by large factors. A stricter reader could still ask for the attribution to be softened.
